This appeal under Section 14-A of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Ac t, 1989 has been filed assailing the orders dated 21.03.2023 passed by learned Special Judge SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, District Shahdol whereby bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. filed on behalf of appellant/accused has been dismissed.

entities.text: Special Judge SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, District Shahdol
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He is in detention since 15.03.2023.

As per the prosecution story, complainant Gopal Singh Gond, who is a member of Scheduled Tribes community, had taken loan from Central Bank, Gohparu, in the year 2003-04 on Kisan Credit Card to purchase a tractor, but he could not pay the loan amount.

Later on, one Rambhushan Pandey,
who is not a member of Scheduled Tribes Community, contacted Gopal Singh Gond and told that number of persons belonging to Scheduled Tribes community are his servants and asked him to execute the sale-deed in favour of one of them.

On his advice, Gopal Singh Gond agreed on his suggestion and thereafter, Gopal Singh Gond and his legal representatives namely Vidur, Sumir Singh, Kunti and Vimla Gond have executed a registered sale-deed in favour of Rambabu Singh Gond S/o Devi Singh Gond and at the time of registry, Babulal Yadav by impersonating himself as Rambabu Singh produced himself as Rambabu Singh and appellant had identified him as Rambabu Singh.
Later on, this fact came to knowledge that no person is residing in the said village Kanchanpur named as Rambabu Singh Gond and thereafter, a case was registered.
Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that appellant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
Appellant has no criminal antecedent.
Therefore, it has been prayed that appellant/accused be released on bail.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed grant of bail to the appellant.
After investigation charge-sheet has been filed.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case,
but without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre trial detention of the appellant/accused is not warranted.
Consequently, appeal stands allowed.

It is directed that appellant - Babulal @ Rambabu Yadav be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount each to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE mrs. mishra Babulal @Rambabau Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59515073/
